notes:
Topline: Large trading platform with latency-sensitive inference paths. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated for reserved capacity (8xA100 baseline) to meet hard latency SLOs across streaming market-data chat and non-streaming batch rerank jobs.

CRM bullets:
- 2026-01-15: Intro AE call (Jordan) — high-level goals, procurement timeline target Apr-26.
- 2026-01-20: Technical discovery w/ SE (Maya) — topology, expected QPS spikes (peak 6k rps for embeddings; 800 rps for chat), target p95 <= 120ms for non-streaming, p95 <= 260ms for streaming end-to-end.
- 2026-02-05: Bench kickoff — initial 24h perf run using sample load generator. Early notes: tail latency sensitive when KV cache misses >10%.
- 2026-02-18: Security review completed — SOC2 docs accepted; asked for KMS integration demo.
- 2026-03-02: SLO alignment call — customer insists on client-side timing definition and wants p99 visibility.
- 2026-03-08: Legal sent SLA markup; asked to clarify uptime credit calculation and multi-region failover commitments.

SLO / measurement details customer wants:
- Definitions requested: p50/p95/p99 measured as client-observed end-to-end time (client call start to final token received) vs server-side token-generation time. They prefer client-side for commercial SLAs but want server-side breakdown for debugging.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: want separate SLOs. Streaming SLOs should define per-chunk latency and final completion time. e.g., median chunk RTT < 60ms, p95 chunk RTT < 220ms, overall completion p95 < 260ms for typical prompts.
- Non-streaming (sync) flows: target p50 45ms, p95 120ms, p99 300ms for sub-512 token requests.
- Measurement windows: rolling 7-day for operational alerts, 30-day for SLA crediting. Agrees to 95th percentile SLA for non-streaming and 99th for streaming end-to-end.
- Timing attribution: want explicit labels — client-side, edge-proxy, routing layer, model-runtime. Ask Redwood to supply traceable spans and token-level timestamps when possible.

Throughput / Reserved GPU planning notes:
- Customer baseline: 8xA100 reserved, ability to burst to 12x for batch rerank nightly window.
- Wants capacity planning run that reports tokens/sec at 512 and 2048 seq lengths and expected KV cache hit effects.
- Concern: autoscaling decisions must be predictable; they want guaranteed throughput per reserved unit and documented degrade modes (fallback model/queueing) when overloaded.

SLA negotiation points (legal):
- Uptime target 99.9% for API control plane; 99.95% for dedicated inference nodes. Credits based on lost compute minutes rather than request failures.
- Definition of incident and maintenance windows; customer insists on 48h notice for planned maintenance affecting single-region capacity.

Open asks for Redwood:
- Provide a clear SLO measurement spec doc that maps observed client-side metrics to server-side traces.
- Run 72h dedicated perf run with varying sequence lengths and streaming enabled; share raw telemetry (percentiles, per-token timelines) and test harness (loadgen config).
- Draft SLA language showing credit calc, maintenance notice, failover commitments.

Customer quote: "We can't absorb unpredictable tail latency during market opens — need hard SLOs and transparent measurement so our ops can automate failover." — Head of Platform

Next action: SE to produce SLO measurement spec and run extended bench (assigned to Maya). Legal to schedule redline sync (Jordan + Legal).
